implement: legion-worker: the phase worker's rules for this repository, the workspace binding, the committed handoff, the push and handoff_complete.
legion-worker/references/pr-body.md: the pull-request body and what a proof entry is; this issue's four acceptance rows each need one, with its own negative control.
legion-worker/references/default-branch-check.md: the App identity of the commits before the first push of this branch.
legion-worker/references/skip-checks-trailer.md: the code push carries no trailer and the handoff-only push does; the daemon classifies a push by its paths, so a wrong trailer stalls the issue.
ce-simplify-code: the resolver branch and the split of newDispatchCloud are settled code by the end of the phase, and the simplify pass runs over them before the pull request is handed on.
dispatch-first and dispatch: a finding outside this issue goes to the controller or the architect, never to a new issue, and a person is reached only through Dispatch.
test: legion-worker: the tester's phase rules, its committed handoff and its evidence.
legion-worker/references/pr-body.md: the rules every phase's evidence follows, so each re-run names its surface, its command, what it observed, the head it ran at and its negative control.

legion-worker/references/tools.md: the gcp package's data-disk tests need mkfs.ext4 and blkid, which a worker pod does not carry and cannot install (uid 1000, the dpkg lock refuses apt-get); this reference is where a tool a role needs comes from, and it decides whether the tester runs the package whole or the filtered command the plan names.
review: legion-worker: the reviewer's phase rules and the finding rules (a clear defect in code this tree touches is fixed in this pull request).
legion-worker/references/review-threads.md: how the reviewer posts, lists and resolves threads and judges a bot's finding.
legion-worker/references/merge-gate.md: the approval of the head by SHA, which the merger's READY compares against.
ce-simplify-code: the reviewer judges whether the simplify pass left the resolver and the cloud split readable, and whether the off path's diff is control flow alone.

findings.finding: A1's preview check cannot run against agent-infra's dispatch/ stack as it stands, and the Summary's "from the same code as production" is not true today: agent-infra pins envoy-infra@2.9.1 in dispatch/Pulumi.yaml and envoy/Pulumi.yaml while this repository's newest release is envoy-infra-v5.4.0, envoy/envoy-infra-version.sh holds every stack to one generated SDK, and this pod carries no pulumi and no gcloud.
findings.answer: The plan's last part, "What this plan does not do, and where it goes", records the pin and the release, states that no stack runs the code this change touches, proves R1 in this repository instead (the registration golden captured before the change, plus the served-schema test), and leaves the stack preview to dispatch://INFRA-775, which moves the pin. Recorded as a spec departure and reported to the architect.

findings.finding: The schema change the work needs is unstated: fifteen inputs are required today, and a generated Go SDK refuses a nil required Input in its constructor before the plugin is called, so a cluster-only program could not call the component at all.
findings.answer: Decision D5 and "Why the schema must change": thirteen inputs become optional in the schema (the Go field types do not move), region and hostname stay required, the resolver keeps today's refusals while clusterOnly is off and refuses each by name while it is on. The consequence for the consumer (seven inputs become *string and need pulumi.StringRef) is listed under "What dispatch://INFRA-775 inherits".

findings.finding: What each of the eight outputs is with the input on is unstated, and one value the consumer already refuses is the empty string.
findings.answer: Decision D4 sets each one: clusterName, kubeconfig and serviceAccountIssuer keep real cluster-derived values, and url, databaseInstance, principal, agentToken and serviceAccountSubject are an explicit empty string, never left unset (an unassigned pulumi.StringOutput awaits as unknown). agent-infra's legion/ program already reads an empty databaseInstance as "dispatch/ has not been applied". The acceptance table asserts all eight through pulumitest.Construct.

findings.finding: "the cluster and its cluster-wide settings" has no referent in the code; the private-services GlobalAddress and servicenetworking Connection are the sharpest case, and the component declares no cluster-wide Kubernetes object.
findings.answer: Decision D2 lists the registrations kept and dropped, resource by resource, and drops the pair with its evidence (their one consumer is the Cloud SQL instance; the cluster declares no relationship to either). The plan states that the mode registers no Kubernetes object at all.

findings.finding: "declares what it declares today" names no baseline a machine can compare against; the existing tests count types alone and would not catch a changed name, parent or order.
findings.answer: Task 1 adds gcp/testdata/dispatch-registrations.golden with one line per registration in order (type, name, parent), committed before the feature so the golden is the pre-change declaration, and the feature commit must leave it byte-identical. Its command and negative control are acceptance row A1b.

findings.finding: A1's first sentence names no checkable set of resources: "Dispatch resource" is undefined.
findings.answer: The Acceptance part states the exact expected set with the input on and the exact zero counts (sql, random, secretmanager, the private-services pair), that no registration's type begins kubernetes:, and that no pulumi:providers:kubernetes is registered.

findings.finding: The input's shape and default are unspecified, and only a plain field with no schema default can work.
findings.answer: Decision D1: ClusterOnly *bool with the tag clusterOnly,optional, plain because Construct refuses another resource's output in a plain field and the value decides which resources register, and no schema default so an applied stack sends no new property. The schema test asserts the shape.

findings.finding: Nothing says what happens if the input is turned on for a stack that already runs Dispatch: it would delete the whole Kubernetes footprint while deletionProtection refuses the Cloud SQL delete.
findings.answer: Decision D5 closes it by construction: such a stack sets the Dispatch inputs, which the mode refuses by name, so the update never starts. The README says so, and the refusal table is tested.

findings.finding: The provider requirement changes for a cluster-only consumer and nothing says so.
findings.answer: Decision D3: the random requirement is skipped in this mode and kept while clusterOnly is off. The acceptance part asserts both.

findings.finding: Claims with no source: R1's "a preview of an existing stack shows no change", A1's preview sentence, the Summary's "from the same code as production", and R1's attribution to dispatch://INFRA-430/spec, whose approved text names no component input.
findings.answer: The plan's last part records the measured pin and release versions and what they make true; the preview claim is answered by the golden and the schema test in this repository, with the live preview named as INFRA-775's. The architect is told, so the spec's own wording stays its owner's to change.

findings.finding: Two in-repository obligations carry no acceptance: the operator document (packages/envoy/infra/README.md records each component's inputs, refusals and resources) and the module's four CI commands.
findings.answer: Task 7 names the README edits (the resource table, the required-inputs sentence, a clusterOnly paragraph) and the changelog fragment; "What CI decides" names the four envoy-infra-go commands, the measured filtered command for a worker pod, and the environmental data-disk failure.

specDepartures.spec: A1: "A preview of agent-infra's dispatch/ stack with the new release shows no change."
specDepartures.plan: R1 is proven in sjawhar/legion by a registration golden captured from the base before the change and left byte-identical by the feature commit, plus a served-schema test that clusterOnly is absent from requiredInputs and that requiredInputs is exactly region and hostname. The preview of agent-infra's stack belongs to dispatch://INFRA-775, which moves agent-infra's pin and already asks for a preview of each stack.
specDepartures.evidence: agent-infra dispatch/Pulumi.yaml and envoy/Pulumi.yaml pin envoy-infra@2.9.1 while this repository's newest release is envoy-infra-v5.4.0, and agent-infra envoy/envoy-infra-version.sh holds every stack to one generated SDK, so no stack runs the code this change touches and a preview after the pin move shows three majors of component change whatever this issue does. The command is also unreachable here: the issue's branch is sjawhar/legion, which cannot carry agent-infra's pin bump, the pod carries no pulumi and no gcloud, and dispatch://INFRA-430/spec records a worker pod taking HTTP 403 on the Pulumi state bucket (measured 2026-10-29).

acceptance: A1's second sentence: the preview of agent-infra's dispatch/ stack is proven by dispatch://INFRA-775 when it moves the pin, not by this issue; this issue proves the declaration identity that makes such a preview show no change.

specDepartures.spec: R1 names one input, off by default, and says nothing about the component's other inputs or about the release this cuts.
specDepartures.plan: Thirteen required inputs become optional in the schema, and every input that configures Dispatch rather than the cluster is refused by name while clusterOnly is on. The pull request's title is feat(envoy-infra)!: so the release is a major, envoy-infra-v6.0.0.
specDepartures.evidence: A generated Go SDK refuses a nil required Input in its constructor before the plugin is called (pkg/codegen/go/gen.go emits the nil check for every required input whose type can be nil), so a cluster-only program could not call the component while tailnetAuthKey, tailnetService, natsUrl, natsSeedSecret and signInClientSecret stay required; nothing on the provider side enforces required-ness, so the refusal must be the resolver's. .github/scripts/release-bump.sh bumps the major version on a subject matching ^[a-z]+(\(.+\))?!:, and seven plain inputs change from string to *string in a regenerated Go SDK.

outcome.scope: The component's input contract changes for every consumer, not only for a cluster-only one: the release is a major, and agent-infra must wrap seven inputs with pulumi.StringRef when it regenerates its SDK.
